indian.headline: Indian markets closed mixed as oil prices and bond yields offset institutional buying support.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed mixed as oil prices and bond yields offset institutional buying support.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 0.55% and Nifty 50 dropped 0.17%, while Bank Nifty gained 0.36%, as crude oil and global yields weighed on sentiment despite ₹9,501 crore of FII and DII inflows.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities ended a three-day losing streak on mixed footing Thursday. The Sensex and Nifty opened higher on strong institutional support—foreign and domestic investors pumped ₹9,501 crore into the market—but the gains proved fragile. Crude oil prices, buoyed by West Asia tensions and hovering above $95 per barrel, and rising US Treasury yields pressured the broader market. By close, the Sensex slid 0.55% and Nifty 50 fell 0.17%, though banking stocks held firmer with Bank Nifty up 0.36%. Sector-wise, banking added 0.4%, but IT dragged with an 0.8% drop and pharma lost 0.5%.

Aside from equity moves, gold and silver surged 1% on MCX as the US dollar and bond yields retreated—a classic safe-haven play. India's 10-year government bond yield briefly tested 7%, signaling rising borrowing costs. On the corporate front, Swiggy's share price fell 2.3% after MSCI removed it from global indices due to new Indian-ownership rules, erasing ₹5,000 crore in market cap. Meanwhile, SoftBank offloaded a 1.7% stake in Meesho for ₹1,650 crore, triggering a 1.3% stock dip. On the IPO front, Lumino Industries is listing today with an estimated 48% premium.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: US bond yields and dollar weakness pulled equities lower; safe-haven demand lifted gold.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: FII and DII together invested ₹9,501 crore; SoftBank exited Meesho stake.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Prices above $95 on West Asia tensions; capped equity gains.

indian.watch: Oil prices and US yields remain key. Watch Lumino Industries debut and Glass Wall IPO next week.

us.headline: US stocks closed higher across all three major indices, with Financials and Healthcare leading gains.
us.lead: US stocks closed higher across all three major indices, with Financials and Healthcare leading gains.
us.brief: S&P 500 rose 0.46%, Nasdaq gained 0.45%, and Dow climbed 0.56% in a broad-based rally.
us.narrative:
US markets ended Wednesday in positive territory as investors digested strong corporate earnings and sector rotation. Financials outperformed with a 0.8% jump, followed by Healthcare at 0.7%, while Tech remained flat. The rally was driven by expanding confidence in AI adoption beyond mega-cap firms—Nvidia climbed on Dell's earnings showing broader AI demand, and Snowflake surged after beating forecasts with AI-fueled growth guidance. Meanwhile, Palantir stumbled despite strong results, pressured by rising bond yields and Google competition, and Broadcom fell even after beating profit expectations.

Globally, South Korea's semiconductor exports more than tripled year-over-year to $46.65 billion in August, signaling robust chip demand but raising concerns about sustainability. In fintech, Microsoft disclosed Azure cloud sales of $101.9 billion annually, and OpenAI revealed it is building automated shutdown capabilities for AI systems after a security incident. For Indian investors, the India-Russia trade update showed 96% of bilateral commerce now settled in rupees and roubles, and two key IT stocks—Hexaware and Persistent Systems—fell on leadership and fundraising news respectively.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Beat earnings, raised AI-driven forecast; stock soared.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Broad rally but caution on bond yields and valuations.

us.watch: Monitor whether AI enthusiasm can sustain if bond yields keep climbing and earnings growth slows.
